summary: Sadananda Das is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Central Sanskrit University (BA 1989) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (MA 1991, PhD 2002), and became a Lecturer at the University of Leipzig in 2005.
Saerji is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has served at Peking University as Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016) and faculty member (attested 2026).
Sagar Uday More works in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Niga Hospital (MBBS, DNB) and was a member of the Epigraphical Society of India in 2025.
Sai Susarla works in computational fields and Indology. He served as Dean at MIT World Peace University (attested 2019) and held a post at the Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation (attested 2025).

Sai Venkatesh Balasubramanian works in Indology and computational fields. He earned a B.Tech (2011) and Ph.D. (2014) from SASTRA, an MBA from Assam Don Bosco University (2014), and was an engineer at IBM India (2011–2012).

Said Reza Huseini specializes in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at JNU (MPhil 2014–2015), King's College London (~2014–2019), Leiden University (BA 2015–2024), and the University of Cambridge (MA 2021–2025).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi (1921–1994) was an Indology and history scholar. Educated at Agra University and under Mohammad Habib, he held posts at Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, AMU, and the Australian National University (Reader, 1967–1986).

Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MPhil at Cardiff University (2014) supervised by Max Deeg, studied under Peter Harvey, and pursued PhD research at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Sakunoshin Motoda (1862–1928) was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Kenyon College (~1888–1891), the University of Pennsylvania (~1892–1895), and Columbia University, later serving at Rikkyo University (~1899–1928).
Sakutaro Fujioka (1870–1910) was a scholar of Japanology and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and later held a post there from circa 1902 to 1910.

Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga (b. 1945) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khenpo Appey Rinpoche, and others, served as Abbot of Sakya Monastery until 2017, and founded Sakya Centre.

Sakyong Mipham (b. 1962) is a scholar and leader in religious and Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, whom he succeeded, and served at Naropa University until 2018.

Sallie B. King (b. 1952) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy. She studied at UBC and under Leon Hurvitz, and served at James Madison University as Professor of Philosophy and Religion (~1992–2016, later Emerita).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (1979), studying under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri, and became Senior Lecturer Emerita at UC Berkeley.

Sally McAra is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000) under Christine Dureau and Karen Nero, and served there as an Honorary Research Fellow in 2019.

Sally Mellick Cutler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford in 1993 and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1996–1997).

Salome Zajadacz-Hastenrath (1932–1998) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She completed her education at Pädagogische Akademie Aachen (1951–1953), the University of Bonn (1956), and the University of Cologne (PhD 1956–1965).

Salomon Lefmann (1831–1912) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Münster, Paris, Heidelberg, and Berlin (PhD under Franz Bopp), and was a professor of Sanskrit at Heidelberg University from 1866 until his death.

Salomon Munk (1803–1867) was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and religion. He studied in Berlin, Bonn, and Paris under scholars including Schlegel and Silvestre de Sacy, later working at the Bibliothèque nationale and the Collège de France.

Salvador Bucca (1920–2005) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore, taught at the National University of Tucumán, and was Professor of Linguistics at Buenos Aires (1955–1983).
